Its composition block carries routing { method: in-loop, version } and definitionHash; its skillMetadata carries the system prompt as website issue 694's ruling C puts it on new records: systemPromptHash inline, and skillText a BlobRef whose stated content hash equals it.

THE BLOBREF. The blob bytes are not in this fixture, and that is the ruled shape: a record carries the BlobRef and the hash, and the text is a separate blob, one per distinct composed prompt. Spec section 9.2 check 17 reads ok on a BlobRef without resolving it (check 9 resolves it), so the record verifies under verify-core 0.15.0 with no fetch.

WHERE THE BYTES COME FROM. This repository's own code: buildCivicAiToolsV1Record() in src/civicaitools-v1-golden.test.ts derives the record from literal inputs with an injected clock and id source, and produce-core assembles it. No record of the reference host declared the subtype when this was written, so the test also asserts the record's structure (the subtype, the content profile, the block key order, the BlobRef and its hash).

REGENERATING. Only when a change is intended to move these bytes: write JSON.stringify(buildCivicAiToolsV1Record().pkg) and the two hashes here, and add a dated line saying what moved and why. The four other fixtures in this directory are not touched by this one.
